messages:
tara (product): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands pricing segment. Posting a concise thread for a few things that didn't get covered live. Please keep Qs short.
maria (sales): For multi-region orgs, how do we meter usage? Some customers deploy in eu + us and want per-region billing.
sam (finance): Default metering is org-global (single invoice). We can enable region-tagged metering on contracts so consumption is broken out by region for chargeback. Requires a small instrumentation flag on the account.
jon (infra): Technically we tag events with region when requests go through our edge. If a customer wants per-region invoices, ops needs to flip "regionized_billing" for the org and we route metering to separate billing buckets.
maria (sales): Is there a minimum commitment or extra fee to enable regionized billing? Customers ask about admin overhead.
sam (finance): No mandatory fee, but we recommend enterprise plans for orgs wanting that level of billing granularity. There is a one-time setup checklist and a short lead time to verify tax/region rules.
tara (product): Question: when we fallback from a large model to a smaller variant during high load, which model's pricing do we bill? Customers want predictability.
jon (infra): We bill the model that actually served the tokens. The fallback model is cheaper. We also emit `X-Model-Served` header so billing reconciliation matches.
sam (finance): To clarify: if a request is proxied to two models (e.g., routing then assembly), we bill both operations by token/time used. We'll include a breakdown in the usage CSV for customers.
quota-bot: Notice: "Org: nebula-tech, regionized_billing not enabled"
maria (sales): How do we handle legacy API keys created before project scoping? Some customers have many old keys and want per-project budgets.
jon (infra): Legacy keys are currently org-scoped. We're rolling out a migration tool that maps keys to projects and allows tagging. The migration is non-destructive and preserves usage history.
tara (product): Is there an automated way to backfill historical usage per-project during migration? Customers need past month split for accounting.
jon (infra): We support best-effort backfills for up to 90 days using inferred routing heuristics; exact splits require customers to add explicit key metadata going forward. We output a migration report you can use for chargeback adjustments.
sam (finance): About credits: can we issue negative credits (i.e., apply a discount post-invoice) for chargeback corrections?
sam (finance): Yes, we can apply adjustments as billing credits or invoice-level discounts. For large adjustments we prefer a credit memo on the next invoice.
tara (product): A couple of policy clarifications: do automatic trial credits apply across replicated regions during a POC?
sam (finance): Trial credits are applied to the org account. If regionized billing is enabled, the trial pool can be split across regions by request; otherwise it's shared.
maria (sales): Customers worry about double metering when they use both hosted Redwood API and our Private control plane connected for metering. Is there deduplication?
jon (infra): We dedupe by request id if the control plane reports identical request ids. Best practice: include a stable request id header so dedupe works across hybrid setups. If dedupe can't be confirmed we bill the received events, so make sure the control plane integrates the SDK's request ids.
tara (product): One last: grandfathered customers on legacy pricing ask if their old rate limits remain the same when they switch to new org model.
sam (finance): We honor grandfathered limits and pricing until the customer agrees to migrate. Any migration will be accompanied by a migration schedule and opt-in.
billing-bot: Billing tip: "Enable regionized_billing via settings or contact finance@redwood.ai to request setup"
tara (product): Thanks all. If you need a follow-up RFC or a small decision ticket for a customer, reply with a single +1 and we'll spin one up.
